To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the organizational form of the transaction affects the restructuring of the firm and that the restructuring actions affect value.

(1) the organizational structure of a highly leveraged transaction has a large effect on the value creation process, (2) the organizational structure employed in a leveraged recapitaliztion is less effective in creating value than that of a leveraged buyout, and (3) the organizational form employed by Safeway in its leveraged buyout was superior to that employed by Kroger in its leveraged recapitaliation.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of organizational form on the restructuring of a company's assets and operations after a HLT.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the form of organizational change associated with an LBO has a significant and positive impact on value creation.
LBO specialists, by altering the organizational form of the acquired company, are able to generate value for the firm and its shareholders that is not available through the leveraged recap process.
the organizational form employed by the LBO specialists at Safeway lead to the creation of more value than the organizational form employed at Kroger.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the form of HLT matters.
the organizational form of the HLT is a key determinant in the restructuring process that occurs following the transaction.
organizational form matters and the choice of organizational form can have important consequences for the firm's ability to generate value.

the choice of organizational form is important in understanding the impact of highly leveraged transactions.
